Citation in original: “Michael R. Otterson, ‘Exploring Questions through Faith and Reasoning,’ BYUI Devotional, Mar. 5, 2013.” When Otterson gave the devotional he was the managing director of LDS Church Public Affairs. This speech has also been titled “Exploring Questions through Faith and Reason.”

The issue of doubt and questioning was receiving a lot of attention both within and outside the church at this time. Kate Kelly, the founder of Ordain Women, was excommunicated a week before this devotional address. In a separate case, creator of the Mormon Stories Podcast John Dehlin had been notified of his own disciplinary council in the previous weeks. Major national publications had articles on these events, leading to much media attention focused on activism and excommunication in the LDS Church. Laurie Goodstein, “Two Activists in Mormon Church Threatened with Excommunication,”New York Times,June 11, 2014; Laurie Goodstein, “Mormons Expel Founder of Group Seeking Priesthood for Women,”New York Times,June 23, 2014. Both Kelly and Dehlin, who was excommunicated in February 2015, made their excommunication letters public. The letters state that neither was excommunicated because they had doubts or questions about the church, but because their public activity was believed to actively erode others’ faith. Michelle Boorstein and Wesley Robinson, “Founder of Mormon Women’s Movement Excommunicated by All-Male Church Panel,”Washington Post,June 23, 2014; Tad Walch, “Mormon Stories Founder Dehlin’s Spread of ‘False Concepts’ Results in Excommunication from LDS Church,”Deseret News,Feb. 10, 2015; “Church Responds to John Dehlin’s Public Comments,”Mormon Newsroom,Feb. 10, 2015.

Citation in original: “Michael R. Otterson, ‘Exploring Questions through Faith and Reasoning,’ BYUI Devotional, Mar. 5, 2013.” Otterson likely borrowed the shelf metaphor from Camilla Kimball. Lavina Fielding,“Camilla Kimball: Lady of Constant Learning,”Ensign5, no. 10 (Oct. 1975): 62. In an 1874 sermon, Brigham Young described using a similar approach regarding the revelation that is nowDoctrine and Covenants 76. “I was not prepared to say that I believed it, and I had to wait. What did I do? I handed this over to the Lord in my feelings, and said I, ‘I will wait until the Spirit of God manifests to me, for or against.’ I did not judge the matter, I did not argue against it. … If I could not see or understand it, I handed it over to the Lord.” Brigham Young, June 23, 1874, inJournal of Discourses,26 vols. (Liverpool: Various publishers, 1855–1886), 18:247.
